item.title: Oh My Opencode Agents: Sisyphus and the Specialist Crew
item.description: The biggest capability jump in OpenCode comes from separating orchestration, planning, execution, and research into specialist agents. Oh My Opencode packages that into a batteries-included harness: Sisyphus coordinating eleven agents with distinct permissions, prompts, and model preferences — where changing an agent’s model changes which prompt fires.

item.title: Text Embeddings for RAG and Search: Ollama and OpenAI-Compatible APIs
item.description: An embedding is a fixed-dimensional float vector placing similar meanings nearby — a representation layer for search, clustering, dedup, and RAG retrieval, not token IDs and not chat output. The concepts stay identical across backends; only the HTTP surface changes. Two local patterns cover nearly everything: Ollama’s embed endpoint and any OpenAI-compatible embeddings route.

item.title: Hermes Agent Memory: Two Small Files Beat a Vector Database
item.description: Models are stateless by design: every request independent, no continuity past the context window. Most frameworks bolt memory on afterward — a database to query, a window to stuff. Hermes inverts it: memory isn’t retrieved when needed but injected at every session start, curated, bounded, always active. Two files under 3,600 characters total.

item.title: Agent Memory Providers Compared: Eight Backends for Persistent Agents
item.description: Assistants forget everything at tab-close unless something persists past the context window. Memory providers — services or libraries holding facts and summaries across sessions, usually wired as plugins — keep the framework thin while memory scales. Eight backends cover the space from zero-dependency local to enterprise cloud.

item.title: Kanban in Hermes: Dispatching Agents Without DDoSing Your Own GPU
item.description: Hermes Agent ships a durable Kanban board whose dispatcher happily promotes every ready task at once — fine against elastic cloud APIs, a self-inflicted denial of service against one small GPU cluster. Uncapped promotion floods the gateway with concurrent requests and turns throughput into queueing, thrashing, and timeouts.

item.title: Cost Optimization for LLM Systems: Spend Tokens Where They Matter
item.description: Ten thousand requests a day at a cent each is $100 daily — and enterprise scale turns that into five figures fast. Optimization isn’t corner-cutting; it’s spending tokens where they matter. Budgets, fallbacks, local inference break-evens, and caching form the practical stack, roughly in that order of effort.

item.title: Model Routing: Stop Using One Model for Everything
item.description: A 70B model summarizing an email burns money; a 3B model reviewing production code courts disaster. Routing matches task complexity to model capability across four strategies — capability, cost, latency, hybrid — each optimizing what hurts most. Production systems converge on hybrid; start there only after one model genuinely fails.

item.title: Open WebUI: Self-Hosted ChatGPT Alternative for Local LLMs
item.description: Open WebUI brings the ChatGPT experience onto your own infrastructure: Ollama plus any OpenAI-compatible backend behind a modern chat UI with RAG document chat, multi-user auth, voice, prompt tooling, and model management. Privacy-first, offline-capable, and scalable from laptop Docker runs to Kubernetes fleets.

item.title: Ollama to vLLM: When Your Local Server Needs to Grow Up
item.description: Ollama is the easiest way to run a local model, until the experiment becomes a shared service. Requests queue, latency wobbles, prefixes recompute, and one GPU stops being enough. vLLM answers exactly those problems — but migration is a trade, not an upgrade: simplicity for scheduling, memory control, parallelism, and production operations.
